headline: President Tinubu Proposes Decriminalization Of Attempted Suicide
seoTitle: Tinubu Seeks To Decriminalize Suicide Attempt
metaDescription: President Bola Tinubu has sent a bill to the Nigerian Senate aiming to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide and provide support for survivors.
aiSummaryBullets: President Bola Tinubu submitted the National Mental Health Amendment Bill 2026 to the Senate.
The proposed legislation seeks to eliminate existing criminal penalties currently applied to individuals who attempt suicide.
The initiative intends to establish a framework that provides constitutional care and support services for survivors of attempted suicide.
aiContextParagraph: President Bola Tinubu has formally requested that the Nigerian Senate review and amend the nation's current legislation regarding suicide. By introducing the National Mental Health Amendment Bill 2026, the administration seeks to move away from the punitive measures that have historically criminalized attempted suicide in Nigeria. The proposed legal framework is designed to transition the focus from criminal prosecution to a system that prioritizes mental health advocacy and recovery for survivors. According to the President, this legislative change is necessary to provide the required constitutional backing to ensure survivors receive appropriate medical care and supportive services rather than facing judicial consequences. The move represents a shift in national policy towards addressing mental health challenges through health-oriented channels rather than legal sanctions, aligning with broader discussions regarding the protection of individuals in vulnerable states of mental distress.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained visibility through coverage by two independent news outlets, demonstrating a moderate level of interest regarding national legislative shifts.
